ne320608923f.s: The Bengal Famine of 1770 is directly linked to which arrangement?
ne320608923f.x: The famine came under the Dual Government (1765-72), when the Company kept squeezing revenue as the famine spread. The Permanent Settlement (1793), Subsidiary Alliance (1798) and Ryotwari came later.

n59a54b11994.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about states accepting Wellesley's Subsidiary Alliance?
o: Scindia accepted it before the Peshwa
n59a54b11994.x: Scindia accepted only in 1804, after the Peshwa (1802); Hyderabad (1798) and Awadh (1801) are correct.

new.s: Under the Dual Government in Bengal, police and criminal justice remained with:
new.x: The Nizamat (police, criminal justice and administration) stayed with the Nawab; the Diwani went to the Company.

new.s: Through which treaty did Shah Alam II grant the Diwani of Bengal, Bihar and Orissa to the Company in 1765?
new.x: The Second Treaty of Allahabad (1765) gave the Company the Diwani in return for a tribute of Rs 26 lakh.

new.s: What annual tribute did the Company agree to pay Shah Alam II for the Diwani in 1765?
new.x: The Company paid Shah Alam II a tribute of Rs 26 lakh; Hastings stopped it after 1772.

new.s: Under the Dual Government, Raja Shitab Rai served as Naib Diwan for:
new.x: Shitab Rai was Naib Diwan of Bihar (Patna); Muhammad Reza Khan handled Bengal at Murshidabad.

new.s: Who was appointed Deputy (Naib) Diwan of Murshidabad by Clive after the Treaty of Allahabad?
new.x: Muhammad Reza Khan was Naib Diwan of Murshidabad (Bengal) and also Naib Nazim.

new.s: Company servants abused private trade in Bengal mainly through misuse of the duty-free:
new.x: Company servants misused the duty-free dastak for private trade; Mir Qasim responded by abolishing internal duties for all.

new.s: Which regions were mainly struck by the Bengal Famine of 1770?
new.x: The famine struck Bengal and Bihar in the lower Gangetic plain in 1769-70.

new.s: Roughly what share of Bengal's population died in the famine of 1770?
new.x: About 7-10 million people died in the 1770 famine, roughly one-third of the population.

new.s: The Company's request for a government loan in 1772 led Parliament to pass the:
new.x: The Company sank into debt and sought a loan in 1772; Parliament intervened with the Regulating Act, 1773.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about the abolition of the Dual Government:
1. It was abolished in 1772 by Warren Hastings.
2. The Calcutta council then acted as Diwan.
3. The tribute to Shah Alam II was increased afterwards.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Hastings abolished it in 1772 and the Calcutta council acted as Diwan; the tribute to Shah Alam II was stopped, not increased.

new.s: The Sanyasi (Fakir) Revolt in Bengal lasted from:
new.x: The Sanyasi-Fakir Revolt ran from 1763 to 1800; the 1770 famine was among its causes.

new.s: Bankim Chandra's Anandamath, set in the 1770 famine, was published in:
new.x: Anandamath appeared in 1882; 1865 is the year of his Durgeshnandini.

new.s: Which of the following was NOT a leader of the Sanyasi-Fakir Revolt?
new.x: Majnum Shah, Bhawani Pathak and Devi Chaudhurani led the revolt; Shah Alam II was the Mughal emperor, not a leader.

new.s: Bankim Chandra's Durgeshnandini (1865) deals with the:
new.x: Durgeshnandini (1865) is set in the Pathan-Mughal conflict of Akbar's reign; Anandamath deals with the famine and Sanyasi revolt.

new.s: Who headed the British side during the Third Anglo-Mysore War (1790-92)?
new.x: Cornwallis led the Third war, which ended with the Treaty of Seringapatam (1792); Wellesley led the Fourth.

new.s: The First Anglo-Mysore War (1767-69) was fought when the Governor of Bengal was:
new.x: Harry Verelst was the British head during the First war, which ended with the Treaty of Madras (1769).

new.s: Under which Governor-General was the Fourth Anglo-Mysore War (1799) fought?
new.x: Lord Wellesley led the Fourth war, in which Srirangapatna fell and Tipu was killed.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Tipu Sultan?
o: He introduced a new calendar and coinage
He discontinued the use of war rockets
He planted a Tree of Liberty at Seringapatam
new.x: Tipu used war rockets; he did not discontinue them. Sericulture, a new calendar, coinage and the Tree of Liberty are all his.

new.s: Besides France, Tipu Sultan sent an embassy to Zaman Shah of:
new.x: Zaman Shah was the ruler of Afghanistan; Tipu also sent envoys to Turkey, Iran, Arabia and Mauritius.

new.s: At the Battle of Pollilur (10 September 1780), Haidar Ali and Tipu defeated:
new.x: At Pollilur Haidar and Tipu beat Col. William Baillie; Coote later beat Haidar at Porto Novo (1781).

new.s: In March 1791, Cornwallis captured which city via Ambur and Vellore?
new.x: Cornwallis took Bangalore in March 1791 during the Third war, advancing via Ambur and Vellore.

new.s: Under the Treaty of Seringapatam (1792), Tipu paid an indemnity of:
new.x: Tipu gave up about half his territory, paid Rs 3 crore and gave two sons as hostages.

new.s: By the Treaty of Seringapatam (1792), the Marathas gained territory around the:
new.x: The Marathas got lands around the Tungabhadra; the Nizam got the Krishna-to-Pennar region.

new.s: Which of the following went to the Nizam under the Treaty of Seringapatam (1792)?
new.x: The Nizam got the Krishna-to-Pennar lands (Bellary, Gurramkonda, Gandikota, Kambham, Kadapa); Malabar, Coorg, Dindigul and Bara Mahal went to the British.

new.s: Which British officers led the 1799 campaign against Seringapatam?
o: General George Harris and Arthur Wellesley
new.x: The 1799 campaign was led by General George Harris with Arthur Wellesley (later Duke of Wellington).

new.s: The Ceded Districts handed to the Company by the Nizam in 1800 were Kadapa, Kurnool, Anantapur and:
new.x: The four Ceded Districts were Kadapa, Kurnool, Anantapur and Bellary, given in 1800 to pay for the subsidiary force.

new.s: During the Second Anglo-Mysore War, the Marathas made peace with the British by the Treaty of:
new.x: The Marathas, first allied with Haidar, made peace with the British at Salbai in 1782.

new.s: What was the Marathas' role in the Fourth Anglo-Mysore War (1799)?
o: They gave no active help to either side
They fought as subsidiary allies of the British
new.x: In 1799 the Nizam was with the British as a subsidiary ally, but the Marathas gave no active help.

new.s: The Gumbaz at Srirangapatna is the:
o: Mausoleum of Haidar Ali and Tipu
new.x: The Gumbaz is the mausoleum of Haidar Ali and Tipu; Daria Daulat Bagh is the summer palace.

new.s: Which of the following was NOT a title of Tipu Sultan?
new.x: Tipu was called Tiger of Mysore, Citizen Tipu and Padshah; Lion of Mysore was not his title.

new.s: Who founded the Asaf Jahi dynasty of Hyderabad?
new.x: Mir Qamar-ud-din Khan, titled Nizam-ul-Mulk Asaf Jah I, founded the dynasty; Mubariz Khan was the Mughal governor he defeated.

new.s: Asaf Jah I began independent rule after defeating Mubariz Khan at Shakar Kheda in:
new.x: He defeated Mubariz Khan at Shakar Kheda on 11 October 1724 and ruled independently from 1724.

new.s: The Secunderabad cantonment is named after which Nizam?
new.x: Secunderabad was named after Sikandar Jah (Asaf Jah III, 1803-29).

new.s: Which treaty of 1768 confirmed the Company's hold over the Northern Circars?
new.x: The Treaty of Masulipatnam (1768) confirmed the Circars; the 1766 Treaty of Hyderabad had leased them.

new.s: The Wahabi conspiracy of 1839 in Hyderabad occurred during the reign of:
new.x: The Wahabi conspiracy (1839), in which Mubariz-ud-Daula was arrested, came under Nasir-ud-Daula (1829-57).

new.s: Salar Jung I, made Diwan of Hyderabad in 1853, was originally named:
new.x: Mir Turab Ali Khan became Diwan on 31 May 1853 after Siraj-ul-Mulk's death and was known as Salar Jung I.

new.s: Turrebaz Khan's attack on the Hyderabad Residency in July 1857 was repulsed by:
new.x: Davidson repulsed Turrebaz Khan's attack of 17 July 1857, made to free Chida Khan.

new.s: In 1759 Salabat Jang gave the British Machilipatnam, Nizampatnam and:
new.x: In 1759 Salabat Jang gave the British Machilipatnam, Nizampatnam, Vakal Mannar and part of Kondapalli.

new.s: Guntur, called the fifth Circar, was also known as:
new.x: Guntur was the fifth Circar, Kondaveedu or Murtazanagar; Mustafanagar was Kondapalli.

new.s: Guntur Circar was handed over to the Company in 1788 for an annual payment of:
new.x: Guntur was handed over on 18 September 1788 for Rs 7 lakh; Rs 9 lakh was the 1766 Circar lease and Rs 15 lakh the proposed figure.

new.s: After which defeat did the Nizam turn to French troops under Raymond, leading to the 1798 alliance?
new.x: Beaten by the Marathas at Kharda (1795), the Nizam blamed Shore's neutrality and turned to French troops under Raymond.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Lord Wellesley and the Subsidiary Alliance?
o: He came to India in 1798 amid the struggle with France
It sought paramountcy without direct administration
He gave the system its final shape
He invented the subsidiary method himself
new.x: Wellesley did not invent the method; he gave it its final shape. The other statements are correct.

new.s: The Peshwa accepted the Subsidiary Alliance by the Treaty of Bassein on:
new.x: The Treaty of Bassein was signed on 31 December 1802, not 1801.

new.s: Which Maratha ruler resisted the Subsidiary Alliance the longest, signing only in 1818?
new.x: Holkar of Indore resisted longest and was the last Maratha to sign (1818); Scindia signed in 1804.

new.s: The Nizam ceded the Ceded Districts to the Company by the treaty of:
new.x: By the treaty of 12 October 1800 the Nizam ceded Kadapa, Kurnool, Anantapur and Bellary in lieu of the subsidy.

new.s: Who proposed the name Rayalaseema for the Ceded Districts in 1928?
new.x: Gadicherla Harisarvottama Rao proposed the name; it was approved at Nandyal under Dr S. Radhakrishnan.

new.s: Who among the following followed the policy of subordinate isolation?
new.x: Lord Hastings (1813-23) followed subordinate isolation; Warren Hastings is linked with the ring-fence policy.

new.s: After 1858, the British policy towards princely states recognised the:
new.x: After 1858 annexation stopped and the right of adoption was recognised.

new.s: Punjab was annexed in 1849 on the ground of:
new.x: Punjab was annexed by conquest after the Second Anglo-Sikh War, and Duleep Singh was deposed.

new.s: Lord Dalhousie abolished the titles and pensions of the rulers of:
new.x: Dalhousie abolished the titles and pensions of the rulers of Tanjore and the Carnatic.

new.s: Which state was annexed under the Doctrine of Lapse in 1849?
new.x: Jaitpur lapsed in 1849; Jaipur was not a lapse case and Gwalior was never annexed.

new.s: Berar was taken from the Nizam in 1853 on the ground of:
new.x: Berar was taken from the Nizam in 1853 for arrears of the subsidy, not under lapse.

new.s: Sindh was annexed by conquest in 1843 under:
new.x: Sindh was conquered in 1843 under Ellenborough (1842-44), before Dalhousie's time.
